name: cavemio-cookie-banner
title: Cookie banner
description: Asks once, plainly, then folds into a small cookie button in the corner that grows back into the preferences.

cavemio.accessibility:
- Nothing optional is on until people say so, and Reject all is as easy and as visible as Accept all, as European regulators expect.
- Browsers that send Global Privacy Control get tracking categories off even on Accept all, with a line saying why.
- A labelled region, not a modal: the page stays usable. Switches are real switches with their descriptions attached; Esc closes the preferences.
- Focus moves with the surface: into the preferences when they open, to the cookie button when it folds.
- The choice is announced when it’s saved. Installs Text morph. With reduced motion the card changes size at once and nothing slides.
cavemio.previewNote: Interactive local fixture. Data and async results are simulated in the preview; the caller supplies application services.

props.name: categories
props.description: Necessary, Analytics, Marketing · Each kind of cookie: id, label, description, and required (always on) or tracking (kept off by Global Privacy Control).

props.name: onConsentChange
props.description: – · Called with the remembered choice on load and with each new one; return a promise and the button waits for it.

props.name: message
props.description: – · The one sentence on the banner.

props.name: policyHref
props.description: – · Adds a "Cookie policy" link after the sentence.

props.name: position
props.description: "bottom-left" · Which corner it sits in and folds into.

props.name: showReopen
props.description: true · Keep the cookie button after a choice. Without it, use openCookiePreferences() from a link.

props.name: expiresAfter
props.description: 365 · Days before asking again. Adding a new kind of cookie asks again too.

props.name: storageKey
props.description: "cookie-consent" · Where the choice is kept in localStorage. getCookieConsent(storageKey) reads it anywhere.

props.name: strategy
props.description: "fixed" · Absolute keeps it inside a positioned parent, as in this preview.

useCases.title: Marketing sites
useCases.description: Ask for consent before analytics or ad scripts run.

useCases.title: SaaS products
useCases.description: Record a visitor’s choices and keep them with your account system.

useCases.title: Sites with EU and UK visitors
useCases.description: A banner where rejecting is as easy as accepting.

useCases.title: Footer “Cookie settings” links
useCases.description: Let people change their mind later from any link on the page.

features.title: Reject is as easy as Accept
features.description: Both buttons are the same size and side by side, and nothing optional is on until people say so.

features.title: Preferences in the same card
features.description: Customise grows the card into a switch for each kind of cookie. Use the defaults or your own categories.

features.title: The choice confirms itself
features.description: While your server records it, the button shows a spinner, then a drawn check and “Accepted”, “Rejected” or “Saved”.

features.title: It folds into a cookie button
features.description: The card shrinks to a small cookie in the corner, or reopens from a footer link with openCookiePreferences().

features.title: It respects Global Privacy Control
features.description: Browsers that send the signal get tracking categories off, even on Accept all, with a line saying why.

features.title: It remembers, and asks again when needed
features.description: The choice is kept for 365 days, and asks again when you add a new kind of cookie.

states.title: ask
states.description: The card rises 20px out of the corner 400ms after the page (640ms). Reject all and Accept all are the same size, side by side.

states.title: customise
states.description: The card’s width and height grow to the preferences (480ms) while the banner blurs out and the preferences blur in. Switch thumbs are thrown with a slight overshoot (400ms). Esc or the close button returns.

states.title: saving
states.description: When onConsentChange returns a promise, the pressed button opens a spinner beside its label until it settles.

states.title: saved
states.description: A check draws itself on the button and the label morphs ("Accepted", "Rejected", "Saved"); after a beat the card shrinks to a 44px circle and the cookie spins in with a small overshoot.

states.title: revisit
states.description: The cookie button, or openCookiePreferences() from a footer link, grows the card back into the preferences. Closing without saving puts the saved choices back.
